Welcome to Team Jiva Yogastro! 🚀✨

​We are taking on the Astronaut Health Monitoring challenge for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. "Jiva" stands for life, and "Yogastro" bridges health, wellness, and aerospace tech. Our goal is to design an intuitive, data-driven health monitoring solution/dashboard to support astronaut well-being on long-duration space missions.

​About Me (Team Lead):

​First-year Computer Science & Engineering (CSE) student.

​Passionate about software development, technology, and space exploration.

​Handling project coordination, software logic, and basic web structure.

​Who We Are Looking For:

We are open to working with passionate teammates of all skill levels! We are especially looking for members interested in:

​UI/UX & Graphic Design (Figma, Canva, or front-end design for sleek astronaut dashboards)

​Research & NASA Data Analysis (Exploring astronaut health parameters, physiological metrics, and space biology datasets)

​Presentation & Pitching (Creating a 7-slide deck and compiling a short pitch video)

​Web/Software Development (HTML/CSS, JavaScript, Python, or prototyping frameworks)

​Whether you are an expert or just starting out like me, if you are enthusiastic about technology, healthcare in space, and building a creative solution together, send a join request! Let's build something impactful. 🌌💻

Project Shunya: Detecting Inside Emptiness in Vast Void Space
Named after the Sanskrit word Shunya—signifying both mathematical zero (zero gravity) and yogic inner stillness—Project Shunya is an offline-ready AI astronaut health monitor that turns a 5-minute daily yoga routine into a non-invasive medical diagnostic tool.
Using onboard camera pose estimation and wearable biometrics (HRV, SpO2, pulse recovery, and skin temperature), it tracks live performance against an astronaut's Earth baseline across four NASA spaceflight health risks: Chair Pose (Utkatasana) for bone and spinal loss, Sun Salutation (Surya Namaskar) for cardiovascular shifts, Bellows Breath (Bhastrika) for immune stress, and Alternate Nostril Breathing & Tree Pose (Nadi Shodhana & Vrikshasana) for isolation burnout and balance loss.
Grounded in NASA OSDR, Standard Measures, and Twins Study data, Project Shunya safeguards astronaut readiness for Artemis and Mars missions.
details:
Project Shunya: Detecting Inside Emptiness in Vast Void Space

1. What It Does & The Story of "Shunya"

Deep-space missions expose astronauts to five extreme hazards: altered gravity, space radiation, isolation, confinement, and hostile closed environments. While current spaceflight hardware tracks physical exercise exertion, subtle early signs of neuromuscular decline, immune stress, and emotional burnout often go unnoticed until symptoms become severe.

Named after the Sanskrit word Shunya—which signifies both mathematical zero (zero gravity) and yogic inner stillness—Project Shunya turns a 5-minute daily yoga routine into a non-invasive, zero-equipment medical diagnostic tool. It helps astronauts detect and counter the "inside emptiness" caused by prolonged isolation while surviving the physical toll of zero gravity.

2. How It Works (Yogic Telemetry & AI)

Project Shunya pairs onboard camera pose estimation with standard wearable biometrics (Heart Rate Variability, SpO2, pulse recovery, and skin temperature) to compare an astronaut's live performance against their pre-flight Earth baseline across four spaceflight health risks:

• Bone & Spinal Degradation (Utkatasana / Chair Pose): Computer vision tracks knee-flexion angle drift, calf/quadriceps micro-tremors, and torso-to-hip spinal alignment to detect antigravity muscle fatigue and microgravity-induced spinal elongation.

• Cardiovascular Adaptations (Surya Namaskar / Sun Salutation): Wearable ECG/PPG sensors measure heart rate spikes, pulse recovery latency, and SpO2 stabilization during slow transitions from horizontal to upright postures to flag orthostatic intolerance and upward fluid shifts.

• Immune System Challenges (Bhastrika Pranayama / Bellows Breath): Analyzes breathing cadence, thoracic expansion symmetry, resting heart rate drift, and skin temperature trends to detect early respiratory fatigue and systemic inflammation before overt illness appears.

• Behavioural Health & Sensorimotor Balance (Nadi Shodhana & Vrikshasana / Alternate Nostril Breathing & Tree Pose): Combines autonomic HRV coherence during breathwork with single-leg balance micro-sway variance during Tree Pose to identify anxiety, sleep disruption, and vestibular disorientation.

3. Scientific Grounding in Official NASA Research

Project Shunya’s diagnostic thresholds and offline-first architecture are grounded directly in peer-reviewed NASA Human Research Program (HRP) investigations:

• NASA Anthropometry and Neutral Body Posture (NBP) Study: Validated our camera-based tracking of joint-angle drift and spinal elongation between pre-flight and in-flight baselines.

• NASA Standard Measures Investigation & NASA Twins Study: Guided our four-pillar multi-system screening across bone formation, arterial remodelling, immune regulation, and cognitive performance.

• NASA Comm Delay Assessment & Neuro Mapping Studies: Informed our autonomous, offline-first alert engine designed for Artemis lunar bases and long-duration Mars transit where real-time Earth communication is delayed.

4. Benefits & Impact

• In Deep Space: Requires zero bulky gym hardware, operates completely offline during communication blackouts, and gives flight surgeons and crew members early Red/Yellow/Green readiness alerts alongside tailored 5-minute recovery flows.

• On Earth: Provides an accessible remote physical therapy, balance screening, and mental wellness monitoring tool for elderly, bedridden, or isolated communities.
